cells.tense: The joining is happening right now and both hands are in it.
cells.ask: Bring one thing only you could bring into the shared thing — a skill, a piece of history, a way of seeing — and let it land as yours.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day, you add your own note to what's being made, and it doesn't get sanded off. It lands, and it changes the thing. Someone can feel you in what's taking shape — present and behind it at the same time, neither holding back nor disappearing.

The direction comes from how engaged you actually are with the thing, not from pressing it. What's free to grow next is your determination — momentum you've gathered, spent defending the call you chose instead of one that was handed to you. Honoring your own pick, standing behind the direction you already took, is the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: You're making something that carries your own stamp, and you know it.
cells.verb: Two streams meeting and deciding to flow as one.
cells.place: Where you become what you actually are.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a version of this that hasn't arrived, and the bracing is doing the deciding.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're involved in produce its result without your hand on it — a meal, a draft, a planted thing — and spend one minute looking at it before you touch it again.
cells.core:
You dream from what's already been lived. The next thing grows out of the last one because the last one got digested, not because you're refusing to look at it. You're tending something that's already growing, and you enjoy what it's become instead of standing over it.

Right now you're rushing the two into one before either has been felt all the way through. What hasn't been digested gets pressed into shape ahead of time, and you call that momentum. The cost is the thing you were joining for — the mix that only happens when both sides are real. The other face of tending is what's called for: growth that doesn't force itself, care that holds without clutching.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing a mix that's already mixing itself.

cells.tense: The choice got made a while back and you're still standing where it was made.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you actually know about where this is headed, and say it to the person it concerns — out loud, once.
cells.core:
You're inside it — showing up to the thing you're making, letting what you know steer your next move, part of the direction instead of watching it from a chair. The vision runs on processed experience, so it has weight, and you trust it enough to walk on it. The joining is a settled fact of the day rather than a conversation still being had, and on a good week you'd be moving with it rather than around it.

What stopped is the meeting. Two strands haven't been brought together, so you're standing in the doorway of your own becoming — close enough to see it, not in it. Start seeing clearly and the current comes back through on its own; don't push feeling into the part that's gone quiet.

cells.tense: You're already becoming it — the pen is down in a room you're writing.
cells.ask: Say 'this is mine' about one piece of what you're growing that you've been crediting to a person, a method, or where you happen to be.
cells.core:
When this part is well, you refine it carefully — not to quiet anything, but because practicing well is itself a kind of connection, and what you refine actually serves the people it touches. Solitude here connects instead of shutting you off.

You're already becoming what you are — it runs in how you spend a day, what you refine, where you put your attention — and you talk about it like it's the practice doing that, or the situation, or luck. The steering is live. Saying so isn't. The earlier, simpler form of the same line is what's needed: mind finding passage, showing the way to one person who needs it.

attempts.check: The draft's most exposed claim is that a second stream is present and unchosen — for Too Much and Too Little the record supports bracing and past-anchoring, not the unread other person, so those cells keep to forgetting the other stream could carry what it carries instead of asserting anything about who is there. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not merged with anyone, I'm alone' — so the ask leans on one chosen act inside a connection they already have, though it's a mild stretch for someone with none. The ask survives being wrong: saying one stream's contribution out loud teaches what joining looks like, whether or not the balance call was accurate. The sentence that flatters the writer is the Too Much opening ('more completely joined than anyone has asked'), which admires its own paradox — it comes out and the plain version stays.
